items.description: 19 of the 20 spec deltas (every change except toolkit-consistency) are plan-roadmap scaffolds whose scenarios are circular: `WHEN <change-id> is implemented THEN <acceptance outcome>`. Each SHALL technically has a WHEN/THEN, but none is verifiable, and all sit under the placeholder capability `multiplayer-collaboration`, for which no `openspec/specs/` directory exists. toolkit-consistency's own plan-findings graded this same pattern 'critical testability' and replaced it. Acceptable as scaffolds that /plan-feature or PLAN_ITERATE must refine, but they must not pass through to IMPLEMENT as-is.

The scaffold generator truncates requirement headings mid-sentence with `...` and lowercases the first character of the outcome, producing `pRs created by` here (and `that given any`, `that /implement-feature` elsewhere). `### Requirement:` headings are the identity used by opsx:sync and by the planned requirement-level collision scanner (ri-06), so truncated, near-identical headings undermine the very collision detection this roadmap introduces.

The rationale for `proposal_approval: auto` is that a recorded `roadmap_approval` already authorizes the plans inside a roadmap. But `proposal_approval` also fires for standalone changes started via /plan-feature or /autopilot with no parent roadmap, where no roadmap_approval exists. As written, the posture removes the only human intent gate for non-roadmap changes, which contradicts the epic's own P3 (intent is an owned artifact) and the fail-closed constraint.

The header comment says 'every failure/escalation path still wait[s] for a human', but `replan_required` (fires when a roadmap item enters `replan_required`, i.e. after a failed plan) is set to `auto`. The table further down is internally consistent (`proposal_approval, replan_required | auto`), so only the comment is wrong, but the comment is what an operator reads first.

Two operator approvals of `escalate_resume` cite a 'cloud single-vendor review policy (TRUST_POSTURE.md 479dcd9)' as their authority. The TRUST_POSTURE.md in this packet contains no review-quorum or single-vendor policy at all; it only defines gate dispositions. Either the policy lives in a commit not present here, or the authority citation is unverifiable from the repository, which defeats P9 traceability. Both approvals also carry `approval_id: null`, so the only record of the human decision is free text in `reason`.

Canonical roadmap state disagrees with the change loop-state. `toolkit-consistency/loop-state.json` shows ri-20 ran GATEKEEPER and PLAN_ITERATE on 2026-10-05 and has been parked in PLAN_REVIEW twice, yet roadmap.yaml still lists ri-20 as `approved` (not `in_progress`), checkpoint.json has no dispatch_attempt for it, `current_item_id` is still ri-01, and roadmap `status` is `planning` after a recorded roadmap_approval proceed. Per docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md roadmap.yaml/loop-state.json are the canonical state a rebuilt queue is projected from, so a reconciliation would re-dispatch ri-20 as fresh work.

The dispatch handshake `launch_token` and lease `owner_nonce` are committed in a tracked file. They appear to be single-use and already consumed (lease state `released`, gate `entered`), so exposure is low, but committing live-looking tokens trains readers to treat them as harmless and will trip secret scanners.

The One-way consumption requirement says merged shared records 'SHALL participate in the existing deduplication', and design.md states that dedupe key is `(capability_gap, affected_skill, session_id)`. But the Exported learning privacy requirement drops `session_id` and allowlists only `event_type, summary, outcome, lessons, tags, created_at`, so neither `session_id` nor top-level `capability_gap`/`affected_skill` exist on an exported record. The exporter's own dedupe key `(capability_gap, affected_skill, summary)` likewise uses two fields that are not in the allowlist. The two requirements cannot both hold unless capability_gap/affected_skill are recovered from tags and the consumer dedupe key is changed.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md Exported learning privacy names capability_gap/affected_skill as retained tag values; One-way consumption dedupes shared records on (capability_gap, affected_skill, summary).

items.description: The privacy requirement drops the `agent_id` and `session_id` fields but exports `tags` verbatim. Per docs/guides/memory-conventions.md, memory entries are tagged with identifiers such as `agent:<id>`, `session:<id>`, `change:<id>` and vendor/model tags, so the identity the allowlist removes re-enters through tags. The secret sanitizer targets credential patterns, not identifiers, so it will not catch this. No scenario covers tag-encoded identity.
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md tags filtered to D4 namespaces; identity/context tags dropped; scenario 'Identity-bearing tags are dropped' added.

items.description: Because the stamp is the pin (D3) and every successful install overwrites it, a teammate who runs install.sh from an un-pinned toolkit checkout silently moves the team's pin instead of hitting drift. The drift check only runs under `--check`. No scenario covers 'install over an existing stamp whose hash differs from the new source', so the implementation is free to overwrite without even a notice; the only safeguard is a git diff on a hash string.

plan-findings.md and session-log.md both claim 25 scenarios; the spec delta contains 26 (Install stamp 4, Payload hash 4, Drift check 6, Shared learnings opt-in 3, Exported learning privacy 4, One-way consumption 3, State-artifact registration 2).
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): plan-findings.md scenario count corrected (26, 27 after finding 9); Iteration 2 section added.

items.description: The record's `written_at` (06:59:55.764) is 35 ms earlier than the `decided_at` of the decision it contains (06:59:55.799), so the file claims to have been written before the decision it records. Two different timestamp formats (`+00:00` vs `Z`) are also used in the same file.

Priority inversion: ri-13 (priority 2) depends on ri-12 (priority 3), so the priority-2 item cannot become ready until a priority-3 item completes. Under the autopilot-roadmap/queue ordering the priority field then misrepresents effective scheduling order.

The Install stamp and Drift check requirements use `<target-root>` for the consumer repository while the Shared learnings and One-way consumption requirements use `<project-root>` for the same directory. Readers may infer two different roots (install target vs the project the exporter runs in).
items.resolution: PLAN_FIX (conductor, inline): spec.md uses <target-root> consistently and defines it once.

items.description: After the operator-approved resume, `escalation_reason` still holds the pre-resume reason, `previous_phase` equals `current_phase`, and `iteration` is 0 while `total_iterations` is 8. Readers of the loop-state cannot tell whether the loop is still escalated or running. Harmless for execution but reduces the state file's value as the canonical record.

Scaffold proposals list dependencies as roadmap item IDs (`ri-02`) rather than change IDs (`ownership-map`). A change proposal is meant to be readable on its own in a PR; a reader without the roadmap cannot resolve `ri-02`. This matters more given the epic's constraint that artifacts stay legible to teammates who do not use the skills.
